title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the 'Théorème-Scholie' begun on p.33. There Grothendieck asks when abstract data (M, ≤, ≪, ‖) come from an 'optimal' atlas satisfying At1–At7, the locus axioms AtL1–AtL3 and AtCL(spec). Here M is a set with two order relations, L is the set of minimal elements, and ‖ is a symmetric antireflexive 'disjointness' relation on L. Page 34 lists the necessary and sufficient conditions.

Notation. omb(X) (the 'ombre', shadow) = {x ∈ L : x ≪ X}. omb(X)^0 (the interior shadow) = {x : x ≪̊ X}. Here x ≪̊ X means x ≪ X, and X is minimal among the X' ≤ X with x ≪ X'.

- ML0 ('trivial axiom'): ≤ ⊆ ≪. The face relation is contained in the adherence/closure relation.
- ML1 (an interpolation or restriction axiom): suppose Z ≪ X, X' ≤ X, and x ∈ L with x ≪ Z and x ≪ X'. Then there is Z' ≤ Z with x ≪ Z' ≪ X'. If moreover Z ≤ X, one may take Z' ≤ X'. In words, adherence relations restrict to faces near a common point, like a frontier or local-structure condition for stratifications.
- ML2: every X has non-empty interior shadow. Every elementary form has an 'open part' not covered by proper faces.
- ML3 ('axiom of minimal structure'): every x in omb(X) lies in the interior shadow of some face X' ≤ X. So omb(X) is the union of the open shadows of its faces, as a closed cell is the disjoint union of the open cells of its faces.
- ML4: ‖ is symmetric and antireflexive. Since this was already assumed in the statement, he later notes it is 'vide' (redundant).
- ML5 (disjunction axiom for loci): if Y ≤ X, y ∈ omb(Y) and x ∈ omb(X) \ omb(Y), then x ‖ y.

NB. ML2 implies that if ≤ = ≪ then M = L. Indeed, x ≪̊ X with x ≤ X forces X = x.

A struck-out passage starts to characterise the atlases themselves as families F ⊂ P(M) satisfying conditions (i), …. The next page carries this out by a free construction Φ: finite, pairwise-compatible subsets of M, ordered by inclusion, with F ≪ G when every element of F is ≪ some element of G. The 'domains' are then the down-closed subfamilies of Φ that are closed under compatible unions.

Purpose: a purely combinatorial, poset-theoretic axiomatisation of the 'atlases' of elementary forms (cells or strata) in the 1986 'Analysis situs' project, which belongs to the tame-topology programme of the Esquisse. The aim is to recover the space-like structure from two order relations and a disjointness relation.
errors: ML4 is redundant given the hypotheses of the Théorème-Scholie; Grothendieck himself notes 'L'axiome ML4 est vide!'.

ML5 as written does not visibly use x ∈ omb(X)^0 versus omb(X), and the role of ‖ on non-distinct-looking points is not clarified on this page. Whether the list ML0–ML5 is really sufficient (the 'il faut et suffit' of p.33) is not proved here; the proof is deferred, and the attempted characterisation of atlases is struck out and restarted on p.35.
The relation ≪ is called an order relation. Antisymmetry of ≪ together with ML0 and ML2 is consistent, but transitivity is used implicitly (omb(Y) ⊆ omb(X) for Y ≤ X).

ideas.what: Axiomatising a 'space' by a set with two orders (face order ≤ and adherence order ≪) plus a disjointness relation on minimal elements
ideas.modern_name: Face posets / abstract stratified sets with frontier condition; Alexandrov-type combinatorial models of stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (finite spaces), Whitney/Thom/Mather (frontier condition), Björner (CW posets); exit-path posets (MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie)
ideas.where_published: Only the programme is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 (tame topology, 'dévissage' of stratified structures); this axiomatics is not published.

ideas.what: Interior shadow omb(X)^0 and the decomposition of omb(X) into the interior shadows of faces (ML2, ML3)
ideas.modern_name: Closed cell = disjoint union of open cells of its faces; regular CW / cellular stratification
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (J.H.C. Whitehead CW complexes; Björner for posets)

ideas.what: Interpolation axiom ML1 (restriction of adherence relations to faces at a common point)
ideas.modern_name: Local conicity / frontier-type compatibility condition for stratifications

ideas.what: Observation that ML2 forces discreteness when ≤ = ≪

missed.claim: Grothendieck states an iff-characterisation (Théorème-Scholie) of the combinatorial data (M, ≤, ≪, ‖) arising from optimal atlases satisfying his locus axioms. He gives the axiom list ML0–ML5 and starts a reconstruction of atlases as families of subsets of M. This is an unpublished combinatorial foundation for his tame-topology 'analysis situs'; it is not developed in the literature as such.
missed.quote: (ML3) ∀ X ∈ M, x ∈ L avec x ≪ X, ∃ X' ≤ X avec x ≪̊ X'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Two-relation poset models (face order plus closure order) parallel current combinatorial models of stratified spaces (exit-path posets, conically smooth or poset-stratified spaces). Comparing Grothendieck's axioms with these could be of historical interest, but the content appears close to known notions.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a detailed, unpublished axiomatics from Grothendieck's 1986 tame-topology project, which is of interest as a record. Mathematically, though, the axioms resemble standard face-poset and stratification conditions, and the page is a list of axioms without deep results.
transcription_corrections: Struck passage near bottom: likely 'Les atlas correspondant à une telle donnée, réalisés comme des ensembles de parties de M, F ⊂ P(M), sont les F satisfaisant les conditions suivantes (i)', not 'Les ateliers correspondant à une label, vérifiés comme des unes en domaine'.
ML1 conclusion: the diagram shows Z' ≤ Z and X' ≤ X with x ≪ Z' ≪ X' (Z' is asserted below Z).
ML2 condition reads '(x ≪ X' ≤ X) ⇒ X' = X'; the subscript after X is spurious.
Margin by ML1 reads approximately 'axiome de suffisance des immersions induites' (uncertain); margin by ML2 approximately 'axiome de divisibilité' (uncertain).
In the NB the redundancy remark reads 'L'axiome ML4 est vide!', consistent with ‖ already being assumed symmetric and antireflexive in the statement on p.33.
